paragraphs.text: Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to draw up a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us,
paragraphs.original: Ἐπειδήπερ πολλοὶ ἐπεχείρησαν ἀνατάξασθαι διήγησιν περὶ τῶν πεπληροφορημένων ἐν ἡμῖν πραγμάτων,
paragraphs.translit: Epeidēper polloi epecheirēsan anataxasthai diēgēsin peri tōn peplērophorēmenōn en hēmin pragmatōn,

paragraphs.text: even as they delivered them unto us, who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word,
paragraphs.original: καθὼς παρέδοσαν ἡμῖν οἱ ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς αὐτόπται καὶ ὑπηρέται γενόμενοι τοῦ λόγου,
paragraphs.translit: kathōs paredosan hēmin hoi apʼ archēs autoptai kai hypēretai genomenoi tou logou,

paragraphs.text: it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus;
paragraphs.original: ἔδοξε κἀμοὶ παρηκολουθηκότι ἄνωθεν πᾶσιν ἀκριβῶς καθεξῆς σοι γράψαι, κράτιστε Θεόφιλε,
paragraphs.translit: edoxe kamoi parēkolouthēkoti anōthen pasin akribōs kathexēs soi grapsai, kratiste Theophile,

paragraphs.text: that thou mightest know the certainty concerning the things wherein thou wast instructed.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα ἐπιγνῷς περὶ ὧν κατηχήθης λόγων τὴν ἀσφάλειαν.
paragraphs.translit: hina epignōs peri hōn katēchēthēs logōn tēn asphaleian.

paragraphs.text: There was in the days of Herod, king of Judaea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abijah: and he had a wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἡρῴδου βασιλέως τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἱερεύς τις ὀνόματι Ζαχαρίας ἐξ ἐφημερίας Ἀβιά, καὶ γυνὴ αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν θυγατέρων Ἀαρών, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς Ἐλισάβετ.
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto en tais hēmerais Hērōdou basileōs tēs Ioudaias hiereus tis onomati Zacharias ex ephēmerias Abia, kai gynē autō ek tōn thygaterōn Aarōn, kai to onoma autēs Elisabet.

paragraphs.text: And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δὲ δίκαιοι ἀμφότεροι ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ, πορευόμενοι ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασιν τοῦ κυρίου ἄμεμπτοι.
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de dikaioi amphoteroi enantion tou theou, poreuomenoi en pasais tais entolais kai dikaiōmasin tou kyriou amemptoi.

paragraphs.text: And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were [now] well stricken in years.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἦν αὐτοῖς τέκνον, καθότι ἦν ἡ Ἐλισάβετ στεῖρα, καὶ ἀμφότεροι προβεβηκότες ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῶν ἦσαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk ēn autois teknon, kathoti ēn hē Elisabet steira, kai amphoteroi probebēkotes en tais hēmerais autōn ēsan.

paragraphs.text: Now it came to pass, while he executed the priest`s office before God in the order of his course,
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἱερατεύειν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ τάξει τῆς ἐφημερίας αὐτοῦ ἔναντι τοῦ θεοῦ
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de en tō hierateuein auton en tē taxei tēs ephēmerias autou enanti tou theou

paragraphs.text: according to the custom of the priest`s office, his lot was to enter into the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
paragraphs.original: κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἱερατείας ἔλαχε τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ κυρίου,
paragraphs.translit: kata to ethos tēs hierateias elache tou thymiasai eiselthōn eis ton naon tou kyriou,

paragraphs.text: And the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the hour of incense.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος ἦν τοῦ λαοῦ προσευχόμενον ἔξω τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ θυμιάματος·
paragraphs.translit: kai pan to plēthos ēn tou laou proseuchomenon exō tē hōra tou thymiamatos·

paragraphs.text: And there appeared unto him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of altar of incense.
paragraphs.original: ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἑστὼς ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ θυμιάματος.
paragraphs.translit: ōphthē de autō angelos kyriou hestōs ek dexiōn tou thysiastēriou tou thymiamatos.

paragraphs.text: And Zacharias was troubled when he saw [him], and fear fell upon him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐταράχθη Ζαχαρίας ἰδών, καὶ φόβος ἐπέπεσεν ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai etarachthē Zacharias idōn, kai phobos epepesen epʼ auton.

paragraphs.text: But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: because thy supplication is heard, and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ ἄγγελος· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Ζαχαρία, διότι εἰσηκούσθη ἡ δέησίς σου, καὶ ἡ γυνή σου Ἐλισάβετ γεννήσει υἱόν σοι, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰωάννην·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de pros auton ho angelos· Mē phobou, Zacharia, dioti eisēkousthē hē deēsis sou, kai hē gynē sou Elisabet gennēsei hyion soi, kai kaleseis to onoma autou Iōannēn·

paragraphs.text: And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔσται χαρά σοι καὶ ἀγαλλίασις, καὶ πολλοὶ ἐπὶ τῇ γενέσει αὐτοῦ χαρήσονται·
paragraphs.translit: kai estai chara soi kai agalliasis, kai polloi epi tē genesei autou charēsontai·

paragraphs.text: For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and he shall drink no wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother`s womb.
paragraphs.original: ἔσται γὰρ μέγας ἐνώπιον τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ οἶνον καὶ σίκερα οὐ μὴ πίῃ, καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου πλησθήσεται ἔτι ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: estai gar megas enōpion tou kyriou, kai oinon kai sikera ou mē piē, kai pneumatos hagiou plēsthēsetai eti ek koilias mētros autou,

paragraphs.text: And many of the children of Israel shall be turn unto the Lord their God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πολλοὺς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐπιστρέψει ἐπὶ κύριον τὸν θεὸν αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: kai pollous tōn hyiōn Israēl epistrepsei epi kyrion ton theon autōn·

paragraphs.text: And he shall go before his face in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient [to walk] in the wisdom of the just; to make ready for the Lord a people prepared [for him].
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτὸς προελεύσεται ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ δυνάμει Ἠλίου, ἐπιστρέψαι καρδίας πατέρων ἐπὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀπειθεῖς ἐν φρονήσει δικαίων, ἑτοιμάσαι κυρίῳ λαὸν κατεσκευασμένον.
paragraphs.translit: kai autos proeleusetai enōpion autou en pneumati kai dynamei Ēliou, epistrepsai kardias paterōn epi tekna kai apeitheis en phronēsei dikaiōn, hetoimasai kyriō laon kateskeuasmenon.

paragraphs.text: And Zacharias said unto the angel, Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife well stricken in years.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν Ζαχαρίας πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον· Κατὰ τί γνώσομαι τοῦτο; ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι πρεσβύτης καὶ ἡ γυνή μου προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen Zacharias pros ton angelon· Kata ti gnōsomai touto; egō gar eimi presbytēs kai hē gynē mou probebēkyia en tais hēmerais autēs.

paragraphs.text: And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God; and I was sent to speak unto thee, and to bring thee these good tidings.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Γαβριὴλ ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἀπεστάλην λαλῆσαι πρὸς σὲ καὶ εὐαγγελίσασθαί σοι ταῦτα·
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis ho angelos eipen autō· Egō eimi Gabriēl ho parestēkōs enōpion tou theou, kai apestalēn lalēsai pros se kai euangelisasthai soi tauta·

paragraphs.text: And behold, thou shalt be silent and not able to speak, until the day that these things shall come to pass, because thou believedst not my words, which shall be fulfilled in their season.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔσῃ σιωπῶν καὶ μὴ δυνάμενος λαλῆσαι ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας γένηται ταῦτα, ἀνθʼ ὧν οὐκ ἐπίστευσας τοῖς λόγοις μου, οἵτινες πληρωθήσονται εἰς τὸν καιρὸν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou esē siōpōn kai mē dynamenos lalēsai achri hēs hēmeras genētai tauta, anthʼ hōn ouk episteusas tois logois mou, hoitines plērōthēsontai eis ton kairon autōn.

paragraphs.text: And the people were waiting for Zacharias, and they marvelled while he tarried in the temple.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἦν ὁ λαὸς προσδοκῶν τὸν Ζαχαρίαν, καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐν τῷ χρονίζειν ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēn ho laos prosdokōn ton Zacharian, kai ethaumazon en tō chronizein en tō naō auton.

paragraphs.text: And when he came out, he could not speak unto them: and they perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple: and he continued making signs unto them, and remained dumb.
paragraphs.original: ἐξελθὼν δὲ οὐκ ἐδύνατο λαλῆσαι αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν ὅτι ὀπτασίαν ἑώρακεν ἐν τῷ ναῷ· καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διανεύων αὐτοῖς, καὶ διέμενεν κωφός.
paragraphs.translit: exelthōn de ouk edynato lalēsai autois, kai epegnōsan hoti optasian heōraken en tō naō· kai autos ēn dianeuōn autois, kai diemenen kōphos.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, when the days of his ministration were fulfilled, he departed unto his house.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto hōs eplēsthēsan hai hēmerai tēs leitourgias autou, apēlthen eis ton oikon autou.

paragraphs.text: And after these days Elisabeth his wife conceived; and she hid herself five months, saying,
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ δὲ ταύτας τὰς ἡμέρας συνέλαβεν Ἐλισάβετ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ· καὶ περιέκρυβεν ἑαυτὴν μῆνας πέντε, λέγουσα
paragraphs.translit: Meta de tautas tas hēmeras synelaben Elisabet hē gynē autou· kai periekryben heautēn mēnas pente, legousa

paragraphs.text: Thus hath the Lord done unto me in the days wherein he looked upon [me], to take away my reproach among men.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι Οὕτως μοι πεποίηκεν κύριος ἐν ἡμέραις αἷς ἐπεῖδεν ἀφελεῖν ὄνειδός μου ἐν ἀνθρώποις.
paragraphs.translit: hoti Houtōs moi pepoiēken kyrios en hēmerais hais epeiden aphelein oneidos mou en anthrōpois.

paragraphs.text: Now in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth,
paragraphs.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀπεστάλη ὁ ἄγγελος Γαβριὴλ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ᾗ ὄνομα Ναζαρὲθ
paragraphs.translit: En de tō mēni tō hektō apestalē ho angelos Gabriēl apo tou theou eis polin tēs Galilaias hē onoma Nazareth

paragraphs.text: to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin`s name was Mary.
paragraphs.original: πρὸς παρθένον ἐμνηστευμένην ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰωσὴφ ἐξ οἴκου Δαυίδ, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς παρθένου Μαριάμ.
paragraphs.translit: pros parthenon emnēsteumenēn andri hō onoma Iōsēph ex oikou Dauid, kai to onoma tēs parthenou Mariam.

paragraphs.text: And he came in unto her, and said, Hail, thou that art highly favored, the Lord [is] with thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰσελθὼν πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπεν· Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ κύριος μετὰ σοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eiselthōn pros autēn eipen· Chaire, kecharitōmenē, ho kyrios meta sou.

paragraphs.text: But she was greatly troubled at the saying, and cast in her mind what manner of salutation this might be.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ διεταράχθη καὶ διελογίζετο ποταπὸς εἴη ὁ ἀσπασμὸς οὗτος.
paragraphs.translit: hē de epi tō logō dietarachthē kai dielogizeto potapos eiē ho aspasmos houtos.

paragraphs.text: And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favor with God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ ἄγγελος αὐτῇ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Μαριάμ, εὗρες γὰρ χάριν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ·
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen ho angelos autē· Mē phobou, Mariam, heures gar charin para tō theō·

paragraphs.text: And behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ συλλήμψῃ ἐν γαστρὶ καὶ τέξῃ υἱόν, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou syllēmpsē en gastri kai texē hyion, kai kaleseis to onoma autou Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Most High: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:
paragraphs.original: οὗτος ἔσται μέγας καὶ υἱὸς Ὑψίστου κληθήσεται, καὶ δώσει αὐτῷ κύριος ὁ θεὸς τὸν θρόνον Δαυὶδ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: houtos estai megas kai hyios Hypsistou klēthēsetai, kai dōsei autō kyrios ho theos ton thronon Dauid tou patros autou,

paragraphs.text: and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.
paragraphs.original: καὶ βασιλεύσει ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰακὼβ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, καὶ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔσται τέλος.
paragraphs.translit: kai basileusei epi ton oikon Iakōb eis tous aiōnas, kai tēs basileias autou ouk estai telos.

paragraphs.text: And Mary said unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ Μαριὰμ πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον· Πῶς ἔσται τοῦτο, ἐπεὶ ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω;
paragraphs.translit: eipen de Mariam pros ton angelon· Pōs estai touto, epei andra ou ginōskō;

paragraphs.text: And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Spirit shall come upon thee, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee: wherefore also the holy thing which is begotten shall be called the Son of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ δύναμις Ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι· διὸ καὶ τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον κληθήσεται, υἱὸς θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis ho angelos eipen autē· Pneuma hagion epeleusetai epi se, kai dynamis Hypsistou episkiasei soi· dio kai to gennōmenon hagion klēthēsetai, hyios theou·

paragraphs.text: And behold, Elisabeth thy kinswoman, she also hath conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month with her that was called barren.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἐλισάβετ ἡ συγγενίς σου καὶ αὐτὴ συνείληφεν υἱὸν ἐν γήρει αὐτῆς, καὶ οὗτος μὴν ἕκτος ἐστὶν αὐτῇ τῇ καλουμένῃ στείρᾳ·
paragraphs.translit: kai idou Elisabet hē syngenis sou kai autē syneilēphen hyion en gērei autēs, kai houtos mēn hektos estin autē tē kaloumenē steira·

paragraphs.text: For no word from God shall be void of power.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι οὐκ ἀδυνατήσει παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πᾶν ῥῆμα.
paragraphs.translit: hoti ouk adynatēsei para tou theou pan rhēma.

paragraphs.text: And Mary said, Behold, the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ Μαριάμ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ δούλη κυρίου· γένοιτό μοι κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου. καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτῆς ὁ ἄγγελος.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de Mariam· Idou hē doulē kyriou· genoito moi kata to rhēma sou. kai apēlthen apʼ autēs ho angelos.

paragraphs.text: And Mary arose in these days and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah;
paragraphs.original: Ἀναστᾶσα δὲ Μαριὰμ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὴν ὀρεινὴν μετὰ σπουδῆς εἰς πόλιν Ἰούδα,
paragraphs.translit: Anastasa de Mariam en tais hēmerais tautais eporeuthē eis tēn oreinēn meta spoudēs eis polin Iouda,

paragraphs.text: and entered into the house of Zacharias and saluted Elisabeth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον Ζαχαρίου καὶ ἠσπάσατο τὴν Ἐλισάβετ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eisēlthen eis ton oikon Zachariou kai ēspasato tēn Elisabet.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤκουσεν τὸν ἀσπασμὸν τῆς Μαρίας ἡ Ἐλισάβετ, ἐσκίρτησεν τὸ βρέφος ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐπλήσθη πνεύματος ἁγίου ἡ Ἐλισάβετ,
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto hōs ēkousen ton aspasmon tēs Marias hē Elisabet, eskirtēsen to brephos en tē koilia autēs, kai eplēsthē pneumatos hagiou hē Elisabet,

paragraphs.text: and she lifted up her voice with a loud cry, and said, Blessed [art] thou among women, and blessed [is] the fruit of thy womb.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀνεφώνησεν κραυγῇ μεγάλῃ καὶ εἶπεν· Εὐλογημένη σὺ ἐν γυναιξίν, καὶ εὐλογημένος ὁ καρπὸς τῆς κοιλίας σου.
paragraphs.translit: kai anephōnēsen kraugē megalē kai eipen· Eulogēmenē sy en gynaixin, kai eulogēmenos ho karpos tēs koilias sou.

paragraphs.text: And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come unto me?
paragraphs.original: καὶ πόθεν μοι τοῦτο ἵνα ἔλθῃ ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ κυρίου μου πρὸς ἐμέ;
paragraphs.translit: kai pothen moi touto hina elthē hē mētēr tou kyriou mou pros eme;

paragraphs.text: For behold, when the voice of thy salutation came into mine ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy.
paragraphs.original: ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡ φωνὴ τοῦ ἀσπασμοῦ σου εἰς τὰ ὦτά μου, ἐσκίρτησεν ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει τὸ βρέφος ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ μου.
paragraphs.translit: idou gar hōs egeneto hē phōnē tou aspasmou sou eis ta ōta mou, eskirtēsen en agalliasei to brephos en tē koilia mou.

paragraphs.text: And blessed [is] she that believed; for there shall be a fulfilment of the things which have been spoken to her from the Lord.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μακαρία ἡ πιστεύσασα ὅτι ἔσται τελείωσις τοῖς λελαλημένοις αὐτῇ παρὰ κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: kai makaria hē pisteusasa hoti estai teleiōsis tois lelalēmenois autē para kyriou.

paragraphs.text: And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἶπεν Μαριάμ· Μεγαλύνει ἡ ψυχή μου τὸν κύριον,
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipen Mariam· Megalynei hē psychē mou ton kyrion,

paragraphs.text: And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠγαλλίασεν τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ τῷ σωτῆρί μου·
paragraphs.translit: kai ēgalliasen to pneuma mou epi tō theō tō sōtēri mou·

paragraphs.text: For he hath looked upon the low estate of his handmaid: For behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me       blessed.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἐπέβλεψεν ἐπὶ τὴν ταπείνωσιν τῆς δούλης αὐτοῦ, ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν μακαριοῦσίν με πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί·
paragraphs.translit: hoti epeblepsen epi tēn tapeinōsin tēs doulēs autou, idou gar apo tou nyn makariousin me pasai hai geneai·

paragraphs.text: For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; And holy is his name.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἐποίησέν μοι μεγάλα ὁ δυνατός, καὶ ἅγιον τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: hoti epoiēsen moi megala ho dynatos, kai hagion to onoma autou,

paragraphs.text: And his mercy is unto generations and generations On them that fear him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ εἰς γενεὰς καὶ γενεὰς τοῖς φοβουμένοις αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai to eleos autou eis geneas kai geneas tois phoboumenois auton.

paragraphs.text: He hath showed strength with his arm; He hath scattered the proud in the imagination of their heart.
paragraphs.original: Ἐποίησεν κράτος ἐν βραχίονι αὐτοῦ, διεσκόρπισεν ὑπερηφάνους διανοίᾳ καρδίας αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: Epoiēsen kratos en brachioni autou, dieskorpisen hyperēphanous dianoia kardias autōn·

paragraphs.text: He hath put down princes from [their] thrones, And hath exalted them of low degree.
paragraphs.original: καθεῖλεν δυνάστας ἀπὸ θρόνων καὶ ὕψωσεν ταπεινούς,
paragraphs.translit: katheilen dynastas apo thronōn kai hypsōsen tapeinous,

paragraphs.text: The hungry he hath filled with good things; And the rich he hath sent empty away.
paragraphs.original: πεινῶντας ἐνέπλησεν ἀγαθῶν καὶ πλουτοῦντας ἐξαπέστειλεν κενούς.
paragraphs.translit: peinōntas eneplēsen agathōn kai ploutountas exapesteilen kenous.

paragraphs.text: He hath given help to Israel his servant, That he might remember mercy
paragraphs.original: ἀντελάβετο Ἰσραὴλ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ, μνησθῆναι ἐλέους,
paragraphs.translit: antelabeto Israēl paidos autou, mnēsthēnai eleous,

paragraphs.text: (As he spake unto our fathers) Toward Abraham and his seed for ever.
paragraphs.original: καθὼς ἐλάλησεν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν, τῷ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
paragraphs.translit: kathōs elalēsen pros tous pateras hēmōn, tō Abraam kai tō spermati autou eis ton aiōna.

paragraphs.text: And Mary abode with her about three months, and returned unto her house.
paragraphs.original: Ἔμεινεν δὲ Μαριὰμ σὺν αὐτῇ ὡς μῆνας τρεῖς, καὶ ὑπέστρεψεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Emeinen de Mariam syn autē hōs mēnas treis, kai hypestrepsen eis ton oikon autēs.

paragraphs.text: Now Elisabeth`s time was fulfilled that she should be delivered; and she brought forth a son.
paragraphs.original: Τῇ δὲ Ἐλισάβετ ἐπλήσθη ὁ χρόνος τοῦ τεκεῖν αὐτήν, καὶ ἐγέννησεν υἱόν.
paragraphs.translit: Tē de Elisabet eplēsthē ho chronos tou tekein autēn, kai egennēsen hyion.

paragraphs.text: And her neighbors and her kinsfolk heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy towards her; and they rejoiced with her.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ περίοικοι καὶ οἱ συγγενεῖς αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐμεγάλυνεν κύριος τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτῆς, καὶ συνέχαιρον αὐτῇ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkousan hoi perioikoi kai hoi syngeneis autēs hoti emegalynen kyrios to eleos autou metʼ autēs, kai synechairon autē.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass on the eighth day, that they came to circumcise the child; and they would have called him Zacharias, after the name of the father.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἦλθον περιτεμεῖν τὸ παιδίον, καὶ ἐκάλουν αὐτὸ ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ Ζαχαρίαν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto en tē hēmera tē ogdoē ēlthon peritemein to paidion, kai ekaloun auto epi tō onomati tou patros autou Zacharian.

paragraphs.text: And his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεῖσα ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Οὐχί, ἀλλὰ κληθήσεται Ἰωάννης.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheisa hē mētēr autou eipen· Ouchi, alla klēthēsetai Iōannēs.

paragraphs.text: And they said unto her, There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτὴν ὅτι Οὐδείς ἐστιν ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου ὃς καλεῖται τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipan pros autēn hoti Oudeis estin ek tēs syngeneias sou hos kaleitai tō onomati toutō.

paragraphs.text: And they made signs to his father, what he would have him called.
paragraphs.original: ἐνένευον δὲ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ τὸ τί ἂν θέλοι καλεῖσθαι αὐτό.
paragraphs.translit: eneneuon de tō patri autou to ti an theloi kaleisthai auto.

paragraphs.text: And he asked for a writing tablet, and wrote, saying, His name is John. And they marvelled all.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αἰτήσας πινακίδιον ἔγραψεν λέγων· Ἰωάννης ἐστὶν ὄνομα αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν πάντες.
paragraphs.translit: kai aitēsas pinakidion egrapsen legōn· Iōannēs estin onoma autou. kai ethaumasan pantes.

paragraphs.text: And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue [loosed], and he spake, blessing God.
paragraphs.original: ἀνεῴχθη δὲ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ παραχρῆμα καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλει εὐλογῶν τὸν θεόν.
paragraphs.translit: aneōchthē de to stoma autou parachrēma kai hē glōssa autou, kai elalei eulogōn ton theon.

paragraphs.text: And fear came on all that dwelt round about them: and all these sayings were noised abroad throughout all the hill country of Judaea.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ πάντας φόβος τοὺς περιοικοῦντας αὐτούς, καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ὀρεινῇ τῆς Ἰουδαίας διελαλεῖτο πάντα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα,
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto epi pantas phobos tous perioikountas autous, kai en holē tē oreinē tēs Ioudaias dielaleito panta ta rhēmata tauta,

paragraphs.text: And all that heard them laid them up in their heart, saying, What then shall this child be? For the hand of the Lord was with him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔθεντο πάντες οἱ ἀκούσαντες ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῶν, λέγοντες· Τί ἄρα τὸ παιδίον τοῦτο ἔσται; καὶ γὰρ χεὶρ κυρίου ἦν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ethento pantes hoi akousantes en tē kardia autōn, legontes· Ti ara to paidion touto estai; kai gar cheir kyriou ēn metʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: And his father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit, and prophesied, saying,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ Ζαχαρίας ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐπλήσθη πνεύματος ἁγίου καὶ ἐπροφήτευσεν λέγων·
paragraphs.translit: Kai Zacharias ho patēr autou eplēsthē pneumatos hagiou kai eprophēteusen legōn·

paragraphs.text: Blessed [be] the Lord, the God of Israel; For he hath visited and wrought redemption for his people,
paragraphs.original: Εὐλογητὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτι ἐπεσκέψατο καὶ ἐποίησεν λύτρωσιν τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Eulogētos kyrios ho theos tou Israēl, hoti epeskepsato kai epoiēsen lytrōsin tō laō autou,

paragraphs.text: And hath raised up a horn of salvation for us In the house of his servant David
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤγειρεν κέρας σωτηρίας ἡμῖν ἐν οἴκῳ Δαυὶδ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai ēgeiren keras sōtērias hēmin en oikō Dauid paidos autou,

paragraphs.text: (As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets that have       been from of old),
paragraphs.original: καθὼς ἐλάλησεν διὰ στόματος τῶν ἁγίων ἀπʼ αἰῶνος προφητῶν αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kathōs elalēsen dia stomatos tōn hagiōn apʼ aiōnos prophētōn autou,

paragraphs.text: Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that       hate us;
paragraphs.original: σωτηρίαν ἐξ ἐχθρῶν ἡμῶν καὶ ἐκ χειρὸς πάντων τῶν μισούντων ἡμᾶς,
paragraphs.translit: sōtērian ex echthrōn hēmōn kai ek cheiros pantōn tōn misountōn hēmas,

paragraphs.text: To show mercy towards, our fathers, And to remember his holy covenant;
paragraphs.original: ποιῆσαι ἔλεος μετὰ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν καὶ μνησθῆναι διαθήκης ἁγίας αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: poiēsai eleos meta tōn paterōn hēmōn kai mnēsthēnai diathēkēs hagias autou,

paragraphs.text: The oath which he spake unto Abraham our father,
paragraphs.original: ὅρκον ὃν ὤμοσεν πρὸς Ἀβραὰμ τὸν πατέρα ἡμῶν, τοῦ δοῦναι ἡμῖν
paragraphs.translit: horkon hon ōmosen pros Abraam ton patera hēmōn, tou dounai hēmin

paragraphs.text: To grant unto us that we being delivered out of the hand       of our enemies Should serve him without fear,
paragraphs.original: ἀφόβως ἐκ χειρὸς ἐχθρῶν ῥυσθέντας λατρεύειν αὐτῷ
paragraphs.translit: aphobōs ek cheiros echthrōn rhysthentas latreuein autō

paragraphs.text: In holiness and righteousness before him all our days.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ὁσιότητι καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ πάσαις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: en hosiotēti kai dikaiosynē enōpion autou pasais tais hēmerais hēmōn.

paragraphs.text: Yea and thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the       Most High: For thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to make ready his       ways;
paragraphs.original: καὶ σὺ δέ, παιδίον, προφήτης Ὑψίστου κληθήσῃ, προπορεύσῃ γὰρ ἐνώπιον κυρίου ἑτοιμάσαι ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai sy de, paidion, prophētēs Hypsistou klēthēsē, proporeusē gar enōpion kyriou hetoimasai hodous autou,

paragraphs.text: To give knowledge of salvation unto his people In the remission of their sins,
paragraphs.original: τοῦ δοῦναι γνῶσιν σωτηρίας τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀφέσει ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν,
paragraphs.translit: tou dounai gnōsin sōtērias tō laō autou en aphesei hamartiōn autōn,

paragraphs.text: Because of the tender mercy of our God, Whereby the dayspring from on high shall visit us,
paragraphs.original: διὰ σπλάγχνα ἐλέους θεοῦ ἡμῶν, ἐν οἷς ἐπισκέψεται ἡμᾶς ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους,
paragraphs.translit: dia splanchna eleous theou hēmōn, en hois episkepsetai hēmas anatolē ex hypsous,

paragraphs.text: To shine upon them that sit in darkness and the shadow of       death; To guide our feet into the way of peace.
paragraphs.original: ἐπιφᾶναι τοῖς ἐν σκότει καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου καθημένοις, τοῦ κατευθῦναι τοὺς πόδας ἡμῶν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰρήνης.
paragraphs.translit: epiphanai tois en skotei kai skia thanatou kathēmenois, tou kateuthynai tous podas hēmōn eis hodon eirēnēs.

paragraphs.text: And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the deserts till the day of his showing unto Israel.
paragraphs.original: Τὸ δὲ παιδίον ηὔξανε καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο πνεύματι, καὶ ἦν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις ἕως ἡμέρας ἀναδείξεως αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: To de paidion ēuxane kai ekrataiouto pneumati, kai ēn en tais erēmois heōs hēmeras anadeixeōs autou pros ton Israēl.
